verses.text: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the sheep gate. They sanctified it, and set up its doors. They sanctified it even to the tower of Hammeah, to the tower of Hananel.
Next to him the men of Jericho built. Next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.
The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate. They laid its beams, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Next to them, Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz made repairs. Next to them, Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel made repairs. Next to them, Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.
Next to them, the Tekoites made repairs; but their nobles didn’t put their necks to the Lord’s work.
Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate. They laid its beams, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
Next to them, Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, repaired the residence of the governor beyond the River.
Next to him, Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs, and they fortified Jerusalem even to the wide wall.
Next to them, Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Next to them, Jedaiah the son of Harumaph made repairs across from his house. Next to him, Hattush the son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hasshub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired another portion, and the tower of the furnaces.
Next to him, Shallum the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, he and his daughters, made repairs.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the valley gate. They built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and one thousand cubits  of the wall to the dung gate.
Malchijah the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem repaired the dung gate. He built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of the district of Mizpah repaired the spring gate. He built it, and covered it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and the wall of the pool of Shelah by the king’s garden, even to the stairs that go down from David’s city.

After him, Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to the place opposite the tombs of David, and to the pool that was made, and to the house of the mighty men.
After him, the Levites, Rehum the son of Bani made repairs. Next to him, Hashabiah, the ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
After him, their brothers, Bavvai the son of Henadad, the ruler of half the district of Keilah made repairs.
Next to him, Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another portion, across from the ascent to the armory at the turning of the wall.
After him, Baruch the son of Zabbai earnestly repaired another portion, from the turning of the wall to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him, Meremoth the son of Uriah the son of Hakkoz repaired another portion, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the end of the house of Eliashib.
After him, the priests, the men of the Plain made repairs.
After them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs across from their house. After them, Azariah the son of Maaseiah the son of Ananiah made repairs beside his own house.
After him, Binnui the son of Henadad repaired another portion, from the house of Azariah to the turning of the wall, and to the corner.

Palal the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the turning of the wall, and the tower that stands out from the upper house of the king, which is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.
(Now the temple servants lived in Ophel, to the place over against the water gate toward the east, and the tower that stands out.)
After him the Tekoites repaired another portion, over against the great tower that stands out, and to the wall of Ophel.
Above the horse gate, the priests made repairs, everyone across from his own house.
After them, Zadok the son of Immer made repairs across from his own house. After him, Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east gate made repairs.
After him, Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another portion. After him, Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs across from his room.
After him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths to the house of the temple servants, and of the merchants, made repairs opposite the gate of Hammiphkad, and to the ascent of the corner.
Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.

footnotes.content: Eliashib the high priest stepped into the work himself—not delegating, but leading. When those who shepherd God's people first take up the hammer and stone, they show what matters most to them. The sheep gate was his station, where sacrifice had always entered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The men of Jericho built next—that old city with the walls that fell. Now they helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall. How the Lord opens new chapters for those willing to work alongside Him, even when their own story once ended in rubble.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Hassenaah took the fish gate. I love how a family name stays with their work—their hands shaped that gate, their faithfulness preserved in the record. Every stone they laid was known to God and now remembered by us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three men, each the son of his father's line—Meremoth, Meshullam, and Zadok all had work assigned them. The Lord loves detail; He notices not just who serves, but whose shoulder was next to whose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Tekoites made repairs, but their nobles wouldn't put their necks to the work. I've seen this everywhere—willing hands and stubborn pride in the same place. The Lord honors those who humble themselves to build, whatever their rank.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joiada and Meshullam repaired the old gate. Old things restored—no shame in that. Sometimes the most faithful work is mending what was broken, not building something new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite worked the governor's residence. Not all were from Jerusalem; the Lord drew strangers to His city's cause. That's always how His kingdom grows—one neighbor at a time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uzziel the goldsmith worked here—a man used to fine, precise work now shaping stone and mortar. Hananiah the perfumer beside him. Every trade, every skill gave itself to the wall. None too high or too low.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rephaiah the ruler didn't rule from above while others labored below. He took his portion of the work. That's what authority looks like when it remembers whom it serves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jedaiah made repairs across from his own house; Hattush next to him. A man guards what lies near his door first. That faithfulness at home spreads outward until the whole city is protected.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Malchijah and Hasshub repaired another portion and the tower of the furnaces. I wonder how many times workers had stood in that tower's heat before—now they were healing it. Faithful hands often heal what they once merely knew.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum the ruler and his daughters made repairs together. Father and daughters, shoulder to shoulder at the wall. Such a simple gift—to pass on faithfulness to the next generation by living it in front of them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hanun and Zanoah's people built the valley gate and a thousand cubits beyond—a massive stretch. Some work calls for more, and faithful servants give it without counting cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Malchijah the son of Rechab repaired the dung gate—not the most honored position, perhaps, yet recorded and remembered forever. The Lord sees who we are in the hard, humble places.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallun repaired the spring gate and the wall of the pool. Living water, David's city—all the old hope and promise flowing through faithful hands again. He covered that gate, built it for permanence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nehemiah the son of Azbuk (a different Nehemiah from our leader) worked opposite David's tombs and the pool. To build in sight of what was, trusting in what will be again—that's faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rehum the Levite made repairs, then Hashabiah worked his own district. The Levites belonged to the Lord first, yet here they were with trowel and stone. Serving at the wall is serving Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bavvai and Henadad, brothers in labor. The Lord loves multiplying the work through faithful pairs and families. Two working as one—that's how kingdoms get built.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezer the ruler of Mizpah worked by the armory, at the turning of the wall. Guardians of weapons, defenders of the city—Ezer helped them with stone what they would guard with courage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baruch 'earnestly repaired'—that one word carries so much. Not dutiful, not grudging, but eager. When a man loves his city and his God, his hands can't work fast enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Meremoth returned—the same man from verse 4, building again. I've noticed faithful servants often appear twice. They don't hide when there's more work. They show up.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests from the Plain brought their strength to the wall. Men of the countryside joining men of the city—that's how a people remember they're one people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin, Hasshub, and Azariah worked across from their own houses. There's such grace in guarding what you know, protecting what you love. That's not narrow—that's faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Binnui of Henadad took a stretch from Azariah's house to the corner. Corners hold cities together—places where two walls meet. Faithful work at the corners, and nothing crumbles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Palal and Pedaiah worked the tower that stood out from the king's house. Built in sight of power, they built it strong. When God's work rises near the centers of earthly rule, His kingdom shows what real strength is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A parenthetical note—the temple servants lived in Ophel. Even a passing word tells us where faithful people dwelled, guarding the holy place. The Lord knew their names and their address.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Tekoites appeared again! This time they worked the great tower and Ophel's wall. The first time they were noted for their nobles' refusal; now they're here again, faithful. Redemption often looks like showing up a second time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Above the horse gate, priests made repairs—each one across from his own house. Again that beautiful pattern: men protecting what they loved. Their faith began at home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zadok across from his house, then Shemaiah the gatekeeper. A man who kept the east gate now helped build the walls it belonged to. He knew what he was guarding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hananiah, Hanun, and Meshullam—names from earlier in the list appearing again. The wall was built by people who came back, who stayed the course. That's what I notice most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Malchijah the goldsmith and merchants worked by the gate of Hammiphkad. Even tradespeople left their shops to build. When a city's walls matter more than goods, you know something true has called them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The goldsmiths and merchants came full circle, from here back to the sheep gate where Eliashib began. Readers today hear an echo in that circle—when God's people labor together, beginning and end meet, and the wall stands whole. We still build like this when we turn from our work to serve something greater.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
